title: Singapore's ScamShield app flags about 5 million suspected scam text messages
summary: ScamShield, a Singapore government app whose on-device machine-learning model filters text messages, flagged about 5 million of them to users as potential scams from March 2022 to November 2023.
account: ScamShield is a Singapore government app by Open Government Products, a unit of GovTech. It was developed with the National Crime Prevention Council and the Singapore Police Force. In June 2021 GovInsider described an on-device machine-learning model that files suspected scam text messages into a junk folder. The app also blocks calls from numbers on a police blocklist. GovInsider reported that users had reported 722,865 text messages and that 5,537 numbers had been blocked since launch. It also reported a claim of 95% detection accuracy. It quoted the product manager, Lennard Lim, on the model's need to adapt as scammers change their attacks. According to The Straits Times, the police had counted 300,500 downloads on iOS in August 2022. On 22 November 2023 the Minister of State Sun Xueling gave an oral reply to parliamentary questions. She said that ScamShield had about 750,000 downloads as of October 2023. She said that about 80,000 unique scam-tainted phone numbers had been blacklisted and blocked. The reply also states that about 5 million text messages had been flagged to users as potential scams. The ministry counts both figures from March 2022. She said that ScamShield had been effective in protecting users. She also cited about 180 million suspected scam calls blocked at network level in the first half of 2023. That figure is a measure by the telecommunications operators and is separate from the app. The Straits Times reported on the same day that the minister said that the app cannot work well unless users set its permissions. The Ministry of Digital Development and Information reported on a page updated on 18 August 2026 that the enhanced app, launched in August 2024, had grown its user base from 944,000 to 1.53 million users. The sources include no evaluation of losses that victims avoided.

She said that ScamShield had been effective in protecting users. She also cited about 180 million suspected scam calls blocked at network level in the first half of 2023. That figure is a measure by the telecommunications operators and is separate from the app. The Straits Times reported on the same day that the minister said that the app cannot work well unless users set its permissions. The Ministry of Digital Development and Information reported on a page updated on 18 August 2026 that the enhanced app, launched in August 2024, had grown its user base from 944,000 to 1.53 million users. fields.account: ScamShield is a Singapore government app by Open Government Products, a unit of GovTech. It was developed with the National Crime Prevention Council and the Singapore Police Force. In June 2021 GovInsider described an on-device machine-learning model that files suspected scam text messages into a junk folder. The app also blocks calls from numbers on a police blocklist. GovInsider reported that users had reported 722,865 text messages and that 5,537 numbers had been blocked since launch. It also reported a claim of 95% detection accuracy. It quoted the product manager, Lennard Lim, on the model's need to adapt as scammers change their attacks. According to The Straits Times, the police had counted 300,500 downloads on iOS in August 2022. On 22 November 2023 the Minister of State Sun Xueling gave an oral reply to parliamentary questions. She said that ScamShield had about 750,000 downloads as of October 2023. She said that about 80,000 unique scam-tainted phone numbers had been blacklisted and blocked. The reply also states that about 5 million text messages had been flagged to users as potential scams. The ministry counts both figures from March 2022. She said that ScamShield had been effective in protecting users. She also cited about 180 million suspected scam calls blocked at network level in the first half of 2023. That figure is a measure by the telecommunications operators and is separate from the app. The Straits Times reported on the same day that the minister said that the app cannot work well unless users set its permissions. The Ministry of Digital Development and Information reported on a page updated on 18 August 2026 that the enhanced app, launched in August 2024, had grown its user base from 944,000 to 1.53 million users. The sources include no evaluation of losses that victims avoided.
